sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate preserves the required direction-selection and inclusive Cf-constant logic and checks the FI formula for every positive-shear calculation case with expected-result-scaled tolerance.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Do not make every nltl:hasCalculationCase node a positive-shear case: remove sh:hasValue nltl:positiveShearForce from the nested shearForceDirection property shape, retain required direction-selection evidence (at least sh:minCount 1, with the canonical direction-value range/class where appropriate), and let the bounded SPARQL rule select only cases whose direction is nltl:positiveShearForce. The current shape incorrectly rejects non-positive calculation cases. Also encode the regulatory Cf constants as equal inclusive bounds in the conditional violation tests (e.g., test failure of factor >= 0.0 && factor <= 0.0, and respectively >= 1.0 && <= 1.0) rather than using != exact-equality comparisons.

Retain the prior direction-selection and inclusive Cf-constant repairs. Amend the bounded SPARQL violation condition so FI = Cf * FIB is checked, using the existing expected-result-scaled tolerance, for every selected positive-shear calculation case, not only when its position falls in the 0.0–0.6LUI or 0.9–1.0LUI regions. Keep the Cf=0.0 and Cf=1.0 conditional violation branches restricted to their respective regions; the formula itself applies along the hull girder and must not be omitted in the intervening region.
Candidate preserves the required direction-selection and inclusive Cf-constant logic and checks the FI formula for every positive-shear calculation case with expected-result-scaled tolerance.
